 # pathland-render-html (Rust) — implementation status
 
-**Last updated:** September 3, 2026
+**Last updated:** September 25, 2026
 
 The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a **stateless, streaming**
 pure function of the opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Each render call
 decodes a self-contained snapshot batch into a **transient** map, walks it once,
 and emits HTML text out — no retained tree, zero cross-call state (Renderer
 Statelessness). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Stateless streaming API**: `HtmlRenderer::render_document(opcodes, strings, root)`
   / `render_fragment(...)` build a transient decode map per call and stream HTML;
   the retained `apply`/`apply_frame`/`render` model is removed.
 - **All spec components render**: `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `COLOR` (layout-greedy:
-  `flex:1;align-self:stretch`), `SHAPE` (CSS/SVG by `SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER`, `SPACER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE`, `VSTACK`/
+  `flex:1;align-self:stretch`), `SHAPE` (CSS/SVG by `SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER`, `SPACER` (inline
+  `flex:1`), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` (`data-min`/`data-max` ride on the gauge so the DOM
+  client can recompute its percentage), `VSTACK`/
   `HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` (flex), `ZSTACK` (overlay), `GRID`/
   `LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` (CSS grid), `SCROLLVIEW`, `BUTTON`, `TEXT_FIELD`
   (incl. `IS_SECURE` → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR`, `TOGGLE`
-  (`TOGGLE_STYLE`), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`, `DATE_PICKER` (`SET_DATE` →
-  `days_to_date`), `PICKER` (option children + `SELECTION`), `MENU`,
+  (`TOGGLE_STYLE`), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER` (the `.pathland-stepper` composite with
+  `data-min`/`data-max`/`data-step` on its hidden range span), `DATE_PICKER` (`SET_DATE` →
+  `days_to_date`), `PICKER` (option children rendered as `<option data-pathland-id="{child}"
+  value="{index}">` + `SELECTION`), `MENU` (the `.pathland-menu` composite:
+  `.pathland-menu-trigger` label + `.pathland-menu-items` children),
   `COLOR_PICKER`, `COMMENT`.
 - **Composite override mode**: `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`SLIDER` with children render
   the custom body wrapped in the native element.
 - **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (cross-axis flex), `CONTENT_MARGINS`,
   `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (`FILL` → `width:100%`/`height:100%` expansion, `HUG` →
   intrinsic), `PADDING` + per-edge, `COLOR`,
   `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT`/`FAMILY`, `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`,
   `Z_INDEX`, `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `BORDER_*`,
   `SELECTED`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`, `ENABLED`, `ROLE`/`STATE` (ARIA), plus
   `TEXT_CASE`, `FONT_STYLE`, `FONT_DESIGN`, `UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH`,
-  `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `COLOR_INVERT`.
+  `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `COLOR_INVERT`. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`
+  `HUG_CONTENT` (-2) is **omitted** (intrinsic size); `FILL` (-1) → `100%`.
+- **ARIA ROLE/STATE maps match the DOM client**: the full `ROLE` set (button…
+  menu, incl. `text`/`img`/`radio`/`spinbutton`/`tablist`/`list`/`grid`/
+  `region`/`menu`) and the `STATE` semantics (one true `aria-*` per state) are
+  canonical with `lib/typescript/src/classes.ts`.
+- **`TREE::INSERT_CHILD` honors its `C` index** (`u32::MAX` = append), matching
+  the protocol and the DOM client's `insertAt`.
 - **Event surfacing**: `data-event-listeners` / `data-action-id` /
   `data-binding-id` attributes.
 - **Navigation slot attrs** (spec DSL.md §4.5 / MODIFIERS.md): a slot node's
   `ROUTE` (STRING) renders as `data-pathland-route="<path>"`, its
   `TRANSITION` hint renders as `data-pathland-transition="<platform|fade|slide|scale>"`,
   its `NAV_CHROME` (F32 enum) renders `data-pathland-nav-chrome="custom"`
   when `Custom` (the renderer adds no default chrome), and `NAV_DEPTH` (U32)
   renders `data-pathland-depth="N"` when deeper than its root so the DOM client
   can hydrate its default back button from the SSR HTML — the DOM renderer
   mirrors the route into the URL, may animate a swap, and draws the renderer's
   own back button (the web has no native navigation container).
 - `STYLE::SET_DATE` handled (days + millis-of-day → date/time).
 - **Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md)**:
+  - The naming/length conventions live in **`src/token_spec.rs`** — the single
+    source of truth consumed by the renderer AND by `pathland-ts-codegen`, which
+    emits the DOM client's `lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`
+    (`tokenToCssVar`, `isDarkToken`, `isLengthToken`, `resolveTokenCssRef`).
   - `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides are collected per snapshot batch and
     emitted into the document head as CSS: base (light) tokens as `:root`
     rules, `dark.*` overrides inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` —
     the browser resolves the scheme natively, so SSR needs no client scheme.
   - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values resolve at render time to
     `var(--pl-…)`, with the generative `space.<N>` family resolving to
     `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)` (`Node::token_ref`).
   - **`STRING`-valued token overrides** (e.g. `font.body.family`): a
     `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` with `valueType = STRING` resolves the value string from
     the batch's string section and emits it single-quoted (escaped) as a
     `:root` rule (or inside the dark media query).
   - The override rules render inside their own **`<style data-pathland-tokens>`**
     element in the document head, **after** the built-in block (so their
     `:root` variables win the cascade and the browser applies them) — matching
     the JS DOM client's `style[data-pathland-tokens]` element. No overrides →
     no extra element.
   - The built-in `:root` tokens use the **canonical spec paths** (`--pl-color-primary`,
     `--pl-color-background`, `--pl-color-text-primary`, `--pl-color-text-secondary`,
     `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-color-border`) so app overrides retheme the
     renderer.
   - **Full Tier-1 default coverage**: `--pl-space-base` (light + dark, so the
     generative `space.<N>` family always resolves), canonical typography
     (`--pl-font-body-size/weight/family`), the radius scale + `--pl-border-width-thin`,
     and the **shared control core mapped onto the canonical catalog** —
     `--pl-control-*`, `--pl-button-*`, `--pl-input-*` (light + dark), with the
     focus ring mapped to `control.accent` and shadows mapped onto the composite
     `elevation.low.*` / `elevation.high.*` tokens. `.pathland-*` rules reference
     the canonical variables, so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides retheme components.
 
 ## Design decision (decision A, September 2026): inline-all + built-in design system
 
 Tailwind is **removed**. The renderer emits **everything inline** as CSS in a
 single `style` attribute — no external compiler, no class system, no safelist:
 
 - **All opcode properties render inline** (`style_css()` + `border_style()`),
   including the previously class-based enum surface (alignment, text alignment,
   text case, visible, font style/design, underline/strikethrough, clips-to-bounds,
   hit-testing, invert, truncation). **1 dp = 1 CSS px**.
 - **`css::STYLE`** is a built-in `<style>` block injected by `render_document`,
   containing:
   - a **preflight reset** (vendored from Tailwind CSS, MIT — see
     `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`),
   - `:root` **design tokens** as CSS custom properties (`--pl-color-primary`,
     `--pl-color-background` (document background), `--pl-color-surface`,
     `--pl-color-text-primary`/`--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-border`,
     `--pl-radius-*`, `--pl-font-sans`, `--pl-input-*` (field bg/text/outline/
     placeholder/focus), button tokens), named to match the canonical protocol
     design-token paths so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` can retheme the renderer,
   - `.pathland-button` (the prettified-button POC, with `prefers-color-scheme`
     dark mode) and `.pathland-*` component defaults (toggle switch, slider, text
     field/editor, stepper, spinner, gauge, menu) — the interactive/hover/focus/
     disabled states that can't be expressed inline. Text fields use a
     Tailwind-style **inset outline** (`outline: 1px solid`, `outline-offset: -1px`,
     focus → `2px`/`-2px` + indigo) instead of a border, with dark-mode tokens;
     `html` sets `color-scheme: light dark` + the `--pl-color-bg` background so
     native form controls and the page follow the theme.
 - **`pathland_html_*` cdylib** (`pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` /
   `_free`) for cross-language hosts (Java JNA shim). The `_tailwind_compile`
   entry point, `tw.rs`, `tailwind.rs`, `build.rs`, `scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs`,
   `vendor/`, and the `tailwind-embed` feature are **deleted**.
 - **Debug comments** (`HtmlRenderer::with_debug_comments(true)`; C ABI
   `pathland_html_render_debug` / `_fragment_debug`): every rendered node is
   prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers
   applied (`<!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill, width=FILL -->`) — values
   decoded by protocol type (FILL/HUG sentinels, well-known enums, colors,
   strings, bitmasks); opt-in so default output is unchanged, and comments stay
   valid HTML (content scrubbed of `--`).
 
+## Cross-renderer conformance (no drift)
+
+The **`pathland-html-golden`** crate renders a battery of scenarios to committed
+fixtures under `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/` (`{name}.plpl` batch bytes +
+`{name}.html` canonical `render_fragment`). Its `tests/guard.rs` fails if the
+SSR output changes without the fixtures being regenerated
+(`cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`), and the TypeScript
+`test/ssr-conformance.test.ts` asserts the DOM client reproduces the same DOM
+from the same batches (fresh-DOM + hydrate-then-delta). The SSR output is the
+contract both renderers must satisfy.
+
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references** cover the directly-mappable subset
   (colors, font size/weight, spacing/padding, corner radius, opacity,
   width/height, border width/color, shadow color). Compound accumulators that
   need concrete numbers (shadow radius/x/y) remain literal-only.
 - `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property).
 - GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact.
 - **Inter is loaded from the rsms.me CDN** (Cloudflare, `font-display: swap`,
   with the InterVariable progressive enhancement for variable-font browsers) —
   the renderer emits the preconnect + stylesheet links in the document head. It
   is **not bundled**: self-hosting a subsetted, OFL-licensed woff2 (embedded in
   the renderer / jar) is a planned follow-up for offline and enterprise
   deployments (see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`).
 
 ## Verified by
 
-`cargo test -p pathland-render-html` — 37 headless render tests (components,

 contents, Inter CDN head links, design tokens: base/dark override CSS, `px`
-lengths, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs, generative `space.N`).
+lengths, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs, generative `space.N`). `cargo test -p
+pathland-html-golden` — the SSR golden-fixture guard.

+//! Generates `lib/typescript/src/constants.ts` from the canonical Rust protocol
+//! constants (`pathland_core::constants`) so the TypeScript DOM renderer's
+//! wire-constant mirror cannot drift: every `export const` below is bound to the
+//! Rust constant it must match, so a rename breaks this crate's compilation and
+//! a revalue changes the emitted file (caught by the CI regen-diff check).
+//!
+//! The enum *codes* (alignment, shape kind, role, state, …) are protocol-semantic
+//! values defined in `spec/MODIFIERS.md`/`spec/OPCODE.md` that today live only in
+//! the specs and the renderers; they are enumerated here so the TS side is
+//! generated rather than hand-mirrored. They are the renderer-facing copy of the
+//! same maps the HTML renderers implement.
+
+use pathland_core::{
+    category, component_type, environment, event, flag, listener, meta, property_id, style, tree,
+    value_type,
+};
+use pathland_render_html::token_spec;
+use std::fmt::Write;
+use std::io;
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+
+/// The canonical source of the emitted file (resolved relative to this crate).
+pub fn constants_ts_path() -> PathBuf {
+    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../../typescript/src/constants.ts")
+}
+
+/// The canonical source of the generated token conventions.
+pub fn tokens_core_ts_path() -> PathBuf {
+    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../../typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts")
+}
+
+fn fmt_u8(v: u8) -> String {
+    format!("{v:#04x}")
+}
+
+fn fmt_u16(v: u16) -> String {
+    format!("{v:#06x}")
+}
+
+fn fmt_u32(v: u32) -> String {
+    format!("{v:#010x}")
+}
+
+fn write_consts(out: &mut String, prefix: &str, items: &[(&str, String)]) {
+    for (name, value) in items {
+        writeln!(out, "export const {prefix}{name} = {value};").unwrap();
+    }
+}
+
+/// The enum-code tables mirrored from `spec/MODIFIERS.md` / `spec/OPCODE.md`.
+/// (These codes are protocol-semantic and have no `pathland_core` consts yet.)
+fn enum_codes() -> Vec<(&'static str, Vec<(&'static str, u32)>)> {
+    vec![
+        ("ALIGN_", vec![("LEADING", 0), ("CENTER", 1), ("TRAILING", 2), ("FILL", 3)]),
+        (
+            "SHAPE_",
+            vec![
+                ("CIRCLE", 0),
+                ("RECTANGLE", 1),
+                ("ROUNDED_RECTANGLE", 2),
+                ("CAPSULE", 3),
+                ("ELLIPSE", 4),
+                ("PATH", 5),
+            ],
+        ),
+        (
+            "TEXT_ALIGN_",
+            vec![("LEADING", 0), ("CENTER", 1), ("TRAILING", 2)],
+        ),
+        (
+            "TRUNCATION_",
+            vec![("HEAD", 0), ("MIDDLE", 1), ("TAIL", 2)],
+        ),
+        ("CONTENT_MODE_", vec![("FIT", 0), ("FILL", 1)]),
+        ("FONT_STYLE_", vec![("NORMAL", 0), ("ITALIC", 1)]),
+        (
+            "FONT_DESIGN_",
+            vec![("DEFAULT", 0), ("SERIF", 1), ("ROUNDED", 2), ("MONOSPACED", 3)],
+        ),
+        ("TEXT_CASE_", vec![("NONE", 0), ("UPPERCASE", 1), ("LOWERCASE", 2)]),
+        (
+            "CONTROL_SIZE_",
+            vec![("SMALL", 0), ("REGULAR", 1), ("LARGE", 2)],
+        ),
+        (
+            "DATE_PICKER_MODE_",
+            vec![("DATE", 0), ("TIME", 1), ("DATE_AND_TIME", 2)],
+        ),

+    writeln!(out, "export const SPACE_FAMILY = {};", q(token_spec::SPACE_FAMILY)).unwrap();

+        "export const LENGTH_PREFIXES: readonly string[] = {};",

+        "export const LENGTH_EXACT: readonly string[] = {};",
+        list(token_spec::LENGTH_EXACT)
+    )

+        "export const LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES: readonly string[] = {};",
+        list(token_spec::LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES)

+    out.push_str(
+        "\n/** The canonical CSS custom property for a token path: `--pl-` prefix, `.` → `-`.\n \
+         *  The `dark.` scheme prefix is stripped — the dark variant overrides the same\n \
+         *  variable inside a media query. */\n\

+         }\n\n\
+         /** Whether a token path selects the dark variant. */\n\
+         export function isDarkToken(path: string): boolean {\n\
+         \x20 return path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX);\n\
+         }\n\n\

+         \x20\x20 if (path.startsWith(prefix)) return true;\n\
+         \x20 }\n\
+         \x20 for (const [prefix, suffix] of LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX) {\n\
+         \x20\x20 if (path.startsWith(prefix) && path.endsWith(suffix)) return true;\n\
+         \x20 }\n\
+         \x20 if (LENGTH_EXACT.includes(path)) return true;\n\
+         \x20 return path.startsWith(\"elevation.\") && LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES.some((s) => path.endsWith(s));\n\

+          *  generative `space.<N>` family resolves to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)`. */\n\
+         export function resolveTokenCssRef(path: string): string {\n\

+         \x20 if (bare.startsWith(SPACE_FAMILY)) {\n\
+         \x20\x20 const rest = bare.slice(SPACE_FAMILY.length);\n\
+         \x20\x20 if (rest.length > 0 && !Number.isNaN(Number(rest))) {\n\
+         \x20\x20\x20 return `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * ${rest})`;\n\
+         \x20\x20 }\n\
+         \x20 }\n\
+         \x20 return `var(${tokenToCssVar(bare)})`;\n\
+         }\n",
+    );

+# pathland-ts-codegen — implementation status
+
+**Last updated:** September 25, 2026
+
+Generates the TypeScript DOM renderer's protocol-derived files from the canonical
+Rust sources, so the TS side cannot drift silently.
+
+## Implemented
+
+- **`constants.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/constants.ts`): every wire constant is
+  bound to its `pathland_core::constants` source (a rename breaks compilation, a
+  revalue changes the emitted file); the protocol-semantic enum codes (alignment,
+  shape kind, role, state, …) are enumerated from `spec/`.
+- **`generated/tokens-core.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`):
+  the design-token conventions (`tokenToCssVar`, `isDarkToken`,
+  `isLengthToken`, `resolveTokenCssRef` + length-token tables) emitted from
+  `pathland_render_html::token_spec` — the single source the Rust renderer and
+  the DOM client share. `src/tokens.ts` imports it.
+- **`npm run regen`** (`lib/typescript/scripts/regen.mjs`) runs both generators
+  (and the golden-fixture emitter); CI's `rust` job runs them and fails on
+  `git diff --exit-code` drift.
+
+## Regenerate

-**Last updated:** September 4, 2026
+**Last updated:** September 25, 2026
 
 The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A vanilla-TypeScript hydration
 client (no runtime dependencies) that is the single source of the client,
 replacing the two duplicated `app.js` files in the demos. Protocol contract:
 `spec/`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Single source, unified**: `src/` is the one client; `npm run build` emits
   `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` (IIFE, minified via esbuild), and
   `npm run copy-to-demos` copies it into both the Quarkus and Spring Boot demos'
   static resource dirs. Both demos serve `/pathland-dom-renderer.js`; the old
   duplicated `app.js` is removed.
 - **Hydration**: builds the `data-pathland-id → element` registry from the SSR
   DOM.
+- **Generated protocol constants** (`src/constants.ts`): emitted by
+  `pathland-ts-codegen` from `pathland_core::constants` (wire constants are bound
+  to the Rust consts; enum codes mirror `spec/`). Regenerate with `npm run regen`;
+  CI (`rust` job) runs the generators and fails on any committed-file drift.
+- **Generated token conventions** (`src/generated/tokens-core.ts`): emitted from
+  `pathland-render-html::token_spec`; `src/tokens.ts` imports them, so the
+  `--pl-*` naming, `dark.` prefix, `space.<N>` family, and length-token rules are
+  single-sourced in Rust.
 - **Logging** (`src/log.ts`, `src/describe.ts`): a tiny **zero-dependency**
   logger (levels + `[pathland:ns]` namespaces, default `info`; opt into
   `debug` with `window.__PATHLAND_LOG_LEVEL="debug"` or
   `?pathland-log=debug`). Meaningful **receive/emit** logging of opcodes and
   events — `→ send EVENT POINTER_UP(target=4, …)`, `← recv frame=7 (2 ops):
   STYLE SET_PROPERTY(ROUTE="/users", …)`, plus lifecycle (connect/reconnect,
   `pushState`, `popstate`, environment) — with a full per-opcode trace at
   `debug` (`src/describe.ts`).
 - **PLPL decode** (`src/plpl.ts`): bounds-checked batch parse — magic/version
   validation, truncated-opcode/string rejection, length-prefixed string reads.
 - **Full delta application** (`src/apply.ts`):
   - **STYLE commands**: `SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_TEXT`, `SET_DATE` (date/time/
     datetime-local), **`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`** (→ CSS variables, `src/tokens.ts`).
   - **TREE commands**: `CREATE_NODE`/`DELETE_NODE`/`INSERT_CHILD`/`REMOVE_CHILD`/
     `MOVE_CHILD` (`u32::MAX` append handled) — the element-shell factory
     (`src/elements.ts`) covers every primitive/control component.
   - **META commands**: `RESET` clears the DOM + registry; `ENVIRONMENT` accepted.

   spec/MODIFIERS.md + control/semantic catalog — layout (spacing/alignment/
   margins/offset/position/frame min-ideal-max/fixed-size/layout-priority/
   aspect-ratio/content-mode), text (align/line-limit/truncation/font-size/

   underline/strikethrough), styling (color/background/border width-color-radius-
   edges/z-index/clips-to-bounds/padding*/tint), effects (shadow/blur/saturation/
   contrast/brightness/grayscale/hue-rotation/color-invert/rotation/scale/
   allows-hit-testing), semantic (role/state/enabled/selected/value/min-max/label/
   prompt), **structural control variants** (is-secure text↔password,
   toggle-style switch↔checkbox↔button, date-picker-mode date↔time↔datetime-local,
   picker-style/control-size as data tokens, step-value, progress/indeterminate),
   binding (action-id/binding-id as `data-*`), image-source, shape-kind.

   handled (`enumCode`/`f32`/`isOn` decoders in classes.ts; token values in
   tokens.ts).

   overrides applied via a managed `<style data-pathland-tokens>` element —
   **base (light) tokens as `:root` rules, `dark.*` overrides inside
   `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`** (so the browser resolves the scheme
   natively and inline-style cascade can't break light mode). Canonical

   to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)` (`applyTokenRefProperty` in classes.ts).
   **`STRING`-valued overrides** (e.g. `font.body.family`) resolve the value
   string from the batch's string section and emit it single-quoted.

   `POINTER_MOVE` (x/y + hover enter/leave), `POINTER_UP` (x/y + secondary),
   `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` (keyCode + modifiers + repeat), `VALUE_CHANGED` (f32 or
   raw bits), `TEXT_CHANGED` (string section), `DATE_CHANGED`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`,
   `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, `WHEEL`, **`NAVIGATE`** (`encodeNavigate`
   URL in the string section + `NAVIGATE_URL` flag; `encodeNavigateBack` no URL),
   and **`META::ENVIRONMENT`** (`encodeEnvironment(width, height, route)`) — guest →
   host (flags `0x0000`).

   `encodeEnvironment` as its **first** WS message (`transport.ts` `onOpen`, before
   any resync) so the server session seeds its router from the `ROUTE` field, and
   re-sends it on `window.resize` to **enrich** the environment after connect
   (viewport + future fields ride the same message).

   (STRING) property updates `data-pathland-route` and fires the `onRoute` hook

   a renderer-side animation of its own output cache — never app state.

   native navigation container, so the DOM renderer draws its own back
   affordance for a `PlatformDefault` nav slot at depth > 1 — a `.pathland-nav-back`
   button injected above the destination when `NAV_DEPTH` (`data-pathland-depth`)
   exceeds 1 and removed at depth 1 / for `Custom` chrome

   from reconcile indexing (`insertAt` skips the class) so TREE deltas never
   displace it; clicking it fires `onNavigateBack`, wired in `src/index.ts` to
   `encodeNavigateBack()` (a `NAVIGATE` back request — the app pops). Hydrated
   once at boot from the SSR HTML via `updateNavBackButtons`.

   existing hydrated element (id already in the registry) and `INSERT_CHILD` skips
   when the child is already in the parent's container — so a resync'd full
   snapshot reconciles against the SSR DOM without clobbering or duplicating.

   nodes carry the same `pathland-*` classes/structure as SSR (a reinstated

Since the `style` variable is still used elsewhere, no unused-var warning. But note: `style_attr` emits ` style="..."` only if non-empty. `combined = format!("flex:1;{css}")` is never empty (always has `flex:1;`), so `style_attr` returns ` style="flex:1;"` (or with css appended). Good.

Scenarios to cover the shell divergence surfaces + composite shells + tokens:
1. `counter` — VStack(Text + Button + Spacer) with spacing/alignment/padding props, text set.
2. `form` — VStack with TextField (label+prompt+secure?), TextEditor, Toggle (switch checked), Slider (value), Button.
3. `composite_controls` — Stepper, Menu, Picker, Gauge, ProgressView (determinate + indeterminate), Divider.
4. `layout` — ZStack, Grid, ScrollView, HStack with width/height FILL/HUG, Color, Shape (rounded rect), Image.

For fragment, token refs resolve to var(--pl-...) inline. The token overrides themselves need render_document to appear. For the golden harness, I should test both render_fragment (client hydration body) and render_document (full doc incl token style). But the TS client hydrates the *body*; the token `<style data-pathland-tokens>` is in the head. The TS `createTokenSink` creates the style element on the client. So for the golden test, the relevant comparison is the *body fragment*. Token overrides in the head are applied via SET_DESIGN_TOKEN deltas on the client through the token sink. 

So for token coverage, the golden scenario should include SET_DESIGN_TOKEN opcodes (which the client applies via applyDesignTokens) + a property with DESIGN_TOKEN ref. The `.html` fixture (fragment) will contain `var(--pl-color-primary)` inline. The client, applying the batch via applyBatch, will: apply SET_DESIGN_TOKEN → token sink creates `<style data-pathland-tokens>`, and apply the DESIGN_TOKEN property → `var(--pl-color-primary)`. Good — the fragment comparison still works for the body.

6. `delta_base` + `delta_change` — base batch and a follow-up delta batch (SET_TEXT + SET_PROPERTY + MOVE_CHILD) to test hydration-then-delta. The harness: TS hydrates `delta_base.html`, applies `delta_change.plpl`, compares resulting DOM to `delta_result.html` (Rust render of base+change snapshot). Rust side: fixture = combined batch rendering.

Let me look at how the render-html tests build opcodes to reuse the pattern. The tests use `Opcode::new(category, command, flags, a, b, c)` and `strings.extend_from_slice(&(len).to_le_bytes())` then the bytes. `strings_str` reads `[u32 len][bytes]` at offset. So when building strings, I need to track offsets for SET_TEXT (B = relative offset), SET_PROPERTY STRING (C = offset), SET_DESIGN_TOKEN (A = offset). Let me create a small builder in the golden lib that manages the string section: `push_str(&mut strings, s) -> u32 offset`. Now let me define scenarios: **Scenario: counter** (VStack root) - root id 1 = VSTACK, spacing 8, alignment center - id 2 = TEXT "Hello" (SET_TEXT) - id 3 = BUTTON text "Tap" - id 4 = SPACER - TREE: create 1,2,3,4; insert 2,3,4 under 1. - STYLE on 1: SPACING 8, ALIGNMENT 1 - STYLE on 2: SET_TEXT "Hello" - STYLE on 3: SET_TEXT "Tap"; EVENT_LISTENERS 4 (pointer up) - (Spacer with no props → flex:1) **Scenario: form** - root 1 = VSTACK spacing 12 - id 2 = TEXT_FIELD, LABEL="Name:", PROMPT="Enter name", SET_TEXT "Bob" - id 3 = TEXT_EDITOR, SET_TEXT "Line1" - id 4 = TOGGLE, SET_TEXT "Enabled", TOGGLE_STYLE 0 (switch), SELECTED 1 - id 5 = SLIDER, SET_TEXT "Volume", MIN_VALUE 0, MAX_VALUE 10, VALUE 5 - insert 2,3,4,5 under 1 **Scenario: composite_controls** - root 1 = VSTACK - id 2 = STEPPER, MIN 0, MAX 10, VALUE 4, STEP 2 - id 3 = MENU, SET_TEXT "Actions" - id 4 = TEXT child "Open" under menu - id 5 = PICKER, SELECTION 1, children 6,7 with text "A","B" - id 8 = GAUGE, MIN 0, MAX 100, VALUE 42 - id 9 = PROGRESS_VIEW, PROGRESS 0.5, MAX 1 - id 10 = PROGRESS_VIEW, IS_INDETERMINATE 1 - id 11 = DIVIDER - insert... **Scenario: layout** - root 1 = ZSTACK - id 2 = COLOR (COLOR red) - id 3 = TEXT "Overlay" - id 4 = SHAPE rounded rect (SHAPE_KIND 2, WIDTH 100, HEIGHT 50, COLOR blue) - id 5 = GRID with WIDTH 2 - id 6 = SCROLLVIEW with child TEXT - id 7 = HSTACK with WIDTH FILL(-1), HEIGHT HUG(-2) - insert children Actually let me keep scenarios a bit more targeted and ensure they exercise the shells: text, button, toggle, slider, stepper, menu, picker, gauge, progress, divider, spacer, stacks, zstack, grid, scrollview, color, shape, textfield, texteditor. That covers the shell table. **Scenario: tokens** - root 1 = VSTACK - id 2 = TEXT "Tokenized" with COLOR DESIGN_TOKEN ref "color.primary", FONT_SIZE DESIGN_TOKEN "font.body.size" - id 3 = TEXT "Spaced" with PADDING DESIGN_TOKEN "space.2" - SET_DESIGN_TOKEN: "color.primary" = COLOR 0xFFFF0000; "dark.color.primary" = COLOR 0xFF0000FF; "font.body.size" = F32 16.0; "space.2" = F32 8.0. Wait — SET_DESIGN_TOKEN uses A=offset(path), B=valueType (u8 low byte), C=value or offset. And the path strings + any string values must be in the string section. Note: for fragment rendering, SET_DESIGN_TOKEN values are collected in Tokens but only render in render_document (head style). render_fragment ignores them (except token refs in properties resolve to var(--pl-...)). For the TS side, applying the batch via applyBatch → applyDesignTokens → token sink. Good. **Scenario: delta (base + change + result)** - base: root 1 = VSTACK with children 2 (TEXT "One"), 3 (TEXT "Two") - change: SET_TEXT on 2 → "Changed"; SET_PROPERTY on 1 SPACING → 16; INSERT_CHILD 4 (new TEXT "Three") under 1 (as last); - result: base+change snapshot rendered. Let me write the opcodes for these. Actually, this is getting long. Let me write the golden crate now. I'll build a small helper to construct opcodes and string arena. Let me define in lib.rs: ```rust pub struct Scenario { pub name: &'static str, pub opcodes: Vec, pub strings: Vec, pub root: u32, } pub struct BatchBuilder { pub opcodes: Vec, pub strings: Vec, } impl BatchBuilder { fn new() -> Self { ... } fn push_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> u32 { let o = self.strings.len() as u32; self.strings.extend_from_slice(&(s.len() as u32).to_le_bytes()); self.strings.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes()); o } fn tree(&mut self, cmd, a, b, c) { self.opcodes.push(Opcode::new(category::TREE, cmd, 0, a, b, c)); } fn style(&mut self, cmd, a, b, c) { ... } fn set_text(&mut self, id, text) { let off = self.push_str(text); self.style(style::SET_TEXT, id, off, 0); } fn set_prop(&mut self, id, vt, prop, value) { self.style(style::SET_PROPERTY, id, ((vt as u32) << 16) | prop as u32, value); } fn create(&mut self, id, component) { self.tree(tree::CREATE_NODE, id, component as u32, 0); } fn insert(&mut self, parent, child) { self.tree(tree::INSERT_CHILD, parent, child, 0); } } ``` Then scenarios: ```rust pub fn scenarios() -> Vec { vec![counter(), form(), composite_controls(), layout(), tokens()] } pub fn delta_scenario() -> DeltaScenario { ... } ``` Emit function: ```rust pub fn fixture_dir() -> PathBuf { Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../typescript/test/fixtures/ssr") } pub fn emit() -> io::Result<()> { write each {name}.plpl and {name}.html; delta_base/change/result } pub fn check() -> Result<(), String> { compare each fixture to current render } ``` For rendering: `HtmlRenderer::new().render_fragment(&opcodes, &strings, root)`. For plpl bytes: `pathland_core_transport::encode_frame(&opcodes, &strings)`. For the delta scenario, the "result" batch is base opcodes + change opcodes concatenated (same strings section? Careful: the delta batch has its own string section with relative offsets. When concatenating for the result snapshot, offsets must remain valid. If I build the delta batch with a *shared* string arena, then base+change strings concatenate fine as long as change's SET_TEXT offsets point into the combined arena. Approach: build base and change with the SAME BatchBuilder strings arena so offsets are consistent across both. The `.plpl` for base = encode_frame(base.opcodes, strings_up_to...) — but encode_frame takes the full strings arena. If base strings contain extra entries not referenced (the change's strings), that's fine — encode_frame encodes the whole strings section; TS readString reads by offset; unused entries are harmless. But the base.html renders with base opcodes only. So: - Build ONE BatchBuilder: base ops + change ops + all strings (offsets consistent). - base.plpl = encode_frame(&base_ops, &all_strings) — includes extra strings, harmless. - base.html = render_fragment(&base_ops, &all_strings, root). - change.plpl = encode_frame(&change_ops, &all_strings) — the delta batch. But wait: the change batch's SET_TEXT offset must be relative to the change batch's string section. Since change.plpl carries the FULL strings arena, the offset is valid. Good. - result.html = render_fragment(&combined_ops, &all_strings, root). Actually for the delta test on the TS side: - Hydrate from base.html (build DOM from HTML). - Apply change.plpl via applyBatch (registry already has nodes 1,2,3 from hydration). SET_TEXT on 2 → setNodeText finds no input/textarea/trigger/.pathland-text → sets el.textContent = "Changed". Good. - SET_PROPERTY SPACING on 1 → el.style.gap = "16px". Good. - CREATE 4 + INSERT_CHILD under 1 → createElement(TEXT) span, insert. Good. - Result: compare serialized to result.html (which has 4 nodes, spacing 16, text changed). But there's an ordering subtlety: `render_fragment` renders children in `children` order. INSERT_CHILD appends. result.html has children 2,3,4. TS inserts 4 at end. Match. Good. One concern: the base.html fixture is the full fragment for the base snapshot. When TS hydrates `document.body.innerHTML = base.html` and registers `[data-pathland-id]` elements — that's exactly what index.ts does. Good. Now the normalizer for TS comparison. Attribute order differences: - Rust SSR: `text` - TS runtime: `setAttribute("data-pathland-id","2")`, then event attrs via handlers, style via el.style. outerHTML serializes attributes in insertion order which may differ. Also happy-dom outerHTML might add `=""` for boolean attrs or normalize styles (e.g. `style="flex: 1;"` vs `flex:1;`). Also attribute quoting, self-closing tags (`` vs ``). The comparison needs normalization: Normalization strategy: parse both strings into DOM via happy-dom, then compare *semantic* trees with a canonicalizer: - Walk the tree, produce a canonical serialization: tag, sorted attributes (excluding style's exact formatting? no — style content matters semantically), text content, children. - For `style`, happy-dom parses into CSSStyleDeclaration; re-serialize via `el.getAttribute("style")`? Better: compare `style` attribute by parsing both into a canonical CSS map (property→value sorted). But happy-dom normalizes some values ("0px" etc.) which the Rust side writes as "0". Hmm. E.g. Rust writes `style="height:0;"` for divider; happy-dom `el.style.height = "0"` → serialized as "height: 0px". So style comparison must normalize numbers: compare via `el.style` property map with value normalization (strip units on zero, trim). This is getting complex but is the crux of making the harness robust. Let me design a canonicalizer that: 1. Parses HTML string → DOM via `document.body.innerHTML = html` in happy-dom (inside a document body). 2. Recursively builds a canonical structure: - For each element: `tag`, then a map of attributes with special handling: - `style`: parse to a sorted list of `prop: value` pairs, normalizing numeric zero ("0px"→"0", "0%"? keep). Also collapse whitespace. - other attributes: `name=value`, sorted. - Text: collapsed whitespace? No — text is significant. Keep as-is but maybe normalize HTML entities (should already be parsed). - Children recursively (including text nodes). Then compare canonical structures. For the delta/hydration test same approach. Actually — simpler and robust enough: since both Rust SSR and TS runtime go through happy-dom parsing on the TS side, and the Rust HTML is deterministic, I can compare canonical structures where style is normalized. Let me implement `canonicalize(el): string` producing a stable string, and assert `canonicalize(parse(ssr)) === canonicalize(parse(tsDom))`. Key style normalizations to handle: - `0` vs `0px` vs `0px`: normalize numeric → trim trailing zeros? Simplest: for style values, map value "0px"/"0" → "0"; "0%"? Leave. Trim whitespace; lowercase property names. - Rust emits `style="flex:1;height:0px"` style strings with `: ` no space and `;` separators; happy-dom serializes `style="flex: 1px; height: 0px"`? Actually happy-dom CSSStyleDeclaration serialization. We'll re-derive from `el.style` property access: iterate `el.style` (CSSStyleDeclaration) properties, get each value. But iterating CSSStyleDeclaration is awkward. Alternative: use `el.getAttribute("style")` and normalize the string: split on `;`, trim, parse `prop:value`, sort, and normalize values (strip spaces, collapse, zero-units). Let me implement: ```ts function normalizeStyle(styleAttr: string): string { const out: string[] = []; for (const decl of styleAttr.split(";")) { const i = decl.indexOf(":"); if (i < 0) continue; const prop = decl.slice(0, i).trim().toLowerCase(); let value = decl.slice(i + 1).trim(); value = value.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim(); value = value.replace(/^0px$/, "0").replace(/^0\./, "0."); // zero px → 0 out.push(`${prop}:${value}`); } out.sort(); return out.join(";"); } ``` Hmm zero handling: Rust emits `height:0px;`? For divider Rust emits `height:0;` (it writes `"height:0;border-top:..."`). happy-dom from `el.style.height = "0"` serializes `height: 0px`. And TS divider shell sets `el.style.borderTop = "1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.2)"`. Rust writes `border-top:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.2);`. Space differences (happy-dom inserts space after colon and between values). normalizeStyle handles spaces. `0px`→`0` handles the zero. Good. Also `display:flex` — happy-dom may serialize as `display: flex`; fine. Also attributes like `data-event-listeners="4"` — same on both. `role="button"` — same. `checked` — happy-dom may serialize as `checked=""`? For checkbox input. Rust writes `checked` (no value). happy-dom serializes boolean attr as `checked` or `checked=""`. My canonicalizer: for attributes, normalize: if value === "" treat specially? I'll produce `name` when value is empty, and `name=value` otherwise. Both would then be `checked`. But Rust writes ` checked` and happy-dom `checked` → canonical `checked`. Good. Also `hidden` attr on stepper range span: Rust writes `hidden`; happy-dom `el.hidden = true` → serializes `hidden`. Good. Also select `selected` on option. Same handling. Now for the canonicalization of the tree — text nodes vs elements. Also the ZSTACK wraps children in `
`. On the TS side, `applyTree` for ZSTACK sets children absolute (per explore: "for ZSTACK parents set position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100% on each child"). Wait — the explore said TS `applyTree` for ZSTACK children sets `position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%` *on each child directly*, whereas Rust SSR wraps each child in a `
`. That's a STRUCTURAL divergence! Let me verify by reading apply.ts. Let me read the applyTree INSERT_CHILD/MOVE_CHILD section.
The golden harness needs a robust DOM normalizer. Let me first check the TS `applyTree` ZSTACK handling to understand a potential structural divergence with the Rust SSR wrapper.

{child}

`. But wait — the wrapper div breaks `byId`/hydration registry? The child node keeps its own `data-pathland-id`. The wrapper is a plain div without an id. `childrenContainer` returns the parent directly (zstack is a plain div). So `insertAt(container, child)` inserts child directly. To wrap, I'd need to create a wrapper and insert the wrapper, then insert the child into the wrapper. But then subsequent INSERT_CHILD deltas for that child's own children still reference the child element (registry maps id→child el), which is inside the wrapper — fine. But `contains` check: `container.contains(child)` — if the child is inside a wrapper inside container, contains returns true. Good for idempotency. However — the hydration case: for SSR, children are already wrapped in `
`. The TS registry hydrates by `data-pathland-id` → the child element (inside the wrapper). On a resync/replay, INSERT_CHILD for the child under the zstack: `container.contains(child)` → true (child is inside wrapper inside container) → skipped. Good. For runtime-created zstack children: need to wrap. Let me change `applyTree` INSERT_CHILD to create a wrapper for ZSTACK children: ```ts if (componentByNode.get(parent) === COMPONENT_ZSTACK && child instanceof HTMLElement) { const wrapper = document.createElement("div"); wrapper.style.position = "absolute"; wrapper.style.inset = "0"; wrapper.appendChild(child); insertAt(container, wrapper, op.c); ... } ``` Wait, but `insertAt` computes visible children — for a zstack, the container's visible children would include the wrappers (elements without nav-back class). Good — insertAt indexes wrappers. And `maybeAnimateInsert(parent, child)` — pass child or wrapper? It animates the inserted child; let me check maybeAnimateInsert. Also `MOVE_CHILD` for zstack children — need to handle wrapping too. Let me keep it consistent: extract a helper `placeChild(container, child, parentComponent, index)` that wraps if zstack. Also — the `contains` guard for a wrapper: after wrapping, `container.contains(child)` is true. On re-insert, we create a NEW wrapper and call insertAt with it — that would duplicate! Need to guard: only wrap if the child is not already contained. The existing guard `if (container && !container.contains(child))` is before the wrapping, so if already contained we skip entirely. Good. But there's a subtlety: MOVE_CHILD does removeChild then insertAt without a contains guard. {child}
` — only position+inset, no width/height. TS previously set width/height 100% on the child. I'll match Rust exactly: wrapper with position:absolute;inset:0 only. Let me check maybeAnimateInsert and then make the edit. Actually, let me reconsider the scope. This ZSTACK divergence is real but is it worth fixing now? The golden harness will flag it in the `layout` scenario. I think fixing it now (as part of Phase 0 alignment) is correct — it's exactly the kind of drift the user wants eliminated. Let me do it. Let me read maybeAnimateInsert.

```rust
//! lib.rs for pathland-html-golden

use pathland_core::{Opcode, category, component_type, property_id, style, tree, value_type};
use pathland_render_html::HtmlRenderer;
use std::io;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// A scenario rendered to a self-contained snapshot: the batch bytes + SSR fragment.
pub struct Scenario {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub batch: Vec<u8>,   // PLPL
    pub html: String,     // render_fragment
    pub root: u32,
}

/// A base → delta pair exercising hydration-then-delta.
pub struct DeltaScenario {
    pub base: Scenario,
    pub change: Vec<u8>, // PLPL delta batch
    pub result: String,  // render_fragment of base + change
    pub root: u32,
}
```

Actually to keep it simple, I'll make the emit function write files:
- `{name}.plpl` and `{name}.html` for each full scenario.
- `delta_base.plpl`, `delta_base.html`, `delta_change.plpl`, `delta_result.html` for the delta scenario.

The `check` function reads those files and compares.

```rust
struct Builder {
    opcodes: Vec<Opcode>,
    strings: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Builder {
    fn new() -> Self { ... }
    fn string(&mut self, s: &str) -> u32 {
        let off = self.strings.len() as u32;
        self.strings.extend_from_slice(&(s.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        self.strings.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
        off
    }
    fn tree(&mut self, command: u8, a: u32, b: u32, c: u32) {
        self.opcodes.push(Opcode::new(category::TREE, command, 0, a, b, c));
    }
    fn style(&mut self, command: u8, a: u32, b: u32, c: u32) {
        self.opcodes.push(Opcode::new(category::STYLE, command, 0, a, b, c));
    }
    fn create(&mut self, id: u32, component: u16) { self.tree(tree::CREATE_NODE, id, component as u32, 0); }
    fn insert(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32) { self.tree(tree::INSERT_CHILD, parent, child, 0); }
    fn set_text(&mut self, id: u32, text: &str) {
        let off = self.string(text);
        self.style(style::SET_TEXT, id, off, 0);
    }
    fn set_prop(&mut self, id: u32, vt: u8, prop: u16, value: u32) {
        self.style(style::SET_PROPERTY, id, ((vt as u32) << 16) | prop as u32, value);
    }
    fn set_string(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, value: &str) {
        let off = self.string(value);
        self.style(style::SET_PROPERTY, id, ((value_type::STRING as u32) << 16) | prop as u32, off);
    }
    fn set_token(&mut self, path: &str, vt: u8, value: u32) {
        let off = self.string(path);
        self.style(style::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN, off, vt as u32, value);
    }
    fn set_date(&mut self, id: u32, days: i32, millis: u32) {
        self.style(style::SET_DATE, id, days as u32, millis);
    }
}
```

The `color:rgba(255,0,0,1)` comes from `style_css()` (COLOR property) plus the inline background-color. That's because the COLOR component reads `property_id::COLOR` for its fill AND `style_css` also emits `color:...` from the COLOR property. Slightly redundant but existing behavior — not a Phase 0 concern.

2. SHAPE id 5: `width:100px;height:50px;...color:rgba(0,0,255,1);width:100px;height:50px;border-radius:8px;border-radius:8px;` — duplicated width/height/color/border-radius. Again existing behavior (the SHAPE base includes width/height/background + css which re-emits). Not a divergence issue since TS applies the same properties via handlers → the same final style. Fine.

3. GRID id 6: `display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr);width:2px;` — the grid WIDTH property is used both for column count AND emitted as width:2px. That's existing behavior (the renderer's style_css emits WIDTH as px). Slightly odd but the TS client would do the same (applyProperty WIDTH sets el.style.width = "2px", and grid shell display:grid + grid-template-columns from the column count handler). state.title: INSERT_CHILD

parts.text:
There's `pathland_core::APPEND` — used in the render-html test as the C value for INSERT_CHILD. So the protocol has an `APPEND` constant. Let me check its value. In TS constants.ts, is there an APPEND? Let me check. The conformance vector says "TREE:INSERT_CHILD (parent=0, child=1, index=MAX)" — so C = index, with a special APPEND/MAX value meaning append.

So the canonical semantics: INSERT_CHILD C = index, where APPEND (probably u32::MAX) means append. Rust `apply_tree` currently ignores C and appends. TS `insertAt` uses op.c directly as an index — but what value do emitters send? The Rust engine emitter and Java emitter send `pathland_core::APPEND` presumably. Let me check the engine's INSERT_CHILD emission and TS's insertAt handling of large index.

parts.text:
The tsconfig has `types: []` (no node types). The existing tests don't use node built-ins. The `process.cwd()` and `node:fs` aren't typed. Options:
1. Add `@types/node` as a dev dep and add `"node"` to tsconfig types — but tsconfig `types: []` is strict. Adding node types could affect the DOM types... Actually `types: []` disables all @types packages. The DOM lib is from `lib` not `@types`. Adding `"node"` to types would pull node globals (process, etc.) which is fine for tests. But `node:fs` module resolution needs the module declaration — `@types/node` provides it.

2. Use vitest's `import.meta.url` + `?raw`? Not binary-safe.

3. Since these are test-only concerns, I could keep tsconfig strict but reference node types via a triple-slash directive in the test file, or use `// @ts-ignore`. Ugly.

Best: add `@types/node` devDependency and add `"node"` to `types` in tsconfig. Let me check the package.json devDeps. Adding @types/node is reasonable for a test suite that reads files.

Actually, tsconfig `types: []` — if I change to `types: ["node"]`, then vitest's globals? The tests import from "vitest" explicitly, so no global types needed. Let me add @types/node.

495:         | property_id::BORDER_COLOR
496:         | property_id::COLOR_VALUE
497:         | property_id::COLOR_MULTIPLY
498:         | property_id::SHADOW_COLOR
499:         | property_id::TINT => value_type::COLOR,

502:         | property_id::IS_SECURE
503:         | property_id::IS_INDETERMINATE

513:         property_id::LABEL
514:         | property_id::PROMPT
515:         | property_id::FONT_FAMILY
516:         | property_id::IMAGE_SOURCE
517:         | property_id::ROUTE => value_type::STRING,
518:         property_id::LINE_LIMIT
519:         | property_id::SELECTION
520:         | property_id::ACTION_ID

522:         | property_id::NAV_DEPTH => value_type::U32,

display.text:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'spec/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  rust:
    name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4 + libadwaita), so the runner
      # needs the GTK4 and libadwaita system libraries before `cargo test` can link them.
      - name: Install GTK4 + libadwaita system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libgtk-4-dev \
            libadwaita-1-dev \
            libglib2.0-dev \
            libcairo2-dev \
            libpango1.0-dev \
            libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
            libgraphene-1.0-dev

      - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: lib/rust -> target

      - name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

      # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
      # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
      # job via an artifact.
      - name: Build the HTML renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
          retention-days: 1

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [rust]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ['17', '21', '25']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      # The renderer jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the rust job). Restore it
      # into the debug dir the jar-embed step copies.
      - name: Download the Rust renderer dylib
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug

      - name: Test reactor (incl. the SSR web demos)
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -q -B test

  web-client:
    name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: lib/typescript/package-lock.json

      - name: Install, typecheck, test, build
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run typecheck
          npm test
          npm run build

      # The demos serve the committed bundle from their static resource dirs;
      # copying the freshly built one must not change the working tree.
      - name: Verify the committed bundle matches the source (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm run copy-to-demos
          git diff --exit-code -- lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/resources

input.newString:
- name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      # The DOM renderer's constants/token conventions and the cross-renderer SSR
      # golden fixtures are GENERATED from Rust (pathland-ts-codegen /
      # pathland-html-golden). Regenerate them here and fail if the committed
      # files drifted — so a renumbered constant or a changed SSR shape can't land
      # without its TS/fixture counterparts.
      - name: Verify generated TS + golden fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen
          cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
          git diff --exit-code -- \
            lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
            lib/typescript/src/generated \
            lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)

69:   and **`META::ENVIRONMENT`** (`encodeEnvironment(width, height, route)`) — guest →
70:   host (flags `0x0000`).

72:   `encodeEnvironment` as its **first** WS message (`transport.ts` `onOpen`, before
73:   any resync) so the server session seeds its router from the `ROUTE` field, and
74:   re-sends it on `window.resize` to **enrich** the environment after connect
75:   (viewport + future fields ride the same message).
76: - **URL mirroring + back/forward** (spec DSL.md §4.5): a slot's `ROUTE`
77:   (STRING) property updates `data-pathland-route` and fires the `onRoute` hook
78:   (`src/index.ts` wires it to `history.pushState` — never called on hydrate, so
79:   no duplicate history entry); `popstate` reports `location.href` as a
80:   `NAVIGATE` event so the app routes. `pushState` never fires `popstate`, so
81:   server-originated navigation cannot loop. **Swap transitions**: a child
82:   inserted into a `data-pathland-transition` slot is animated in (fade/slide/
83:   scale keyframes injected once into a `<style data-pathland-transitions>`),
84:   a renderer-side animation of its own output cache — never app state.

86:   native navigation container, so the DOM renderer draws its own back

88:   button injected above the destination when `NAV_DEPTH` (`data-pathland-depth`)
89:   exceeds 1 and removed at depth 1 / for `Custom` chrome
90:   (`data-pathland-nav-chrome="custom"`, `NAV_CHROME=1`). The button is excluded
91:   from reconcile indexing (`insertAt` skips the class) so TREE deltas never
92:   displace it; clicking it fires `onNavigateBack`, wired in `src/index.ts` to
93:   `encodeNavigateBack()` (a `NAVIGATE` back request — the app pops). Hydrated
94:   once at boot from the SSR HTML via `updateNavBackButtons`.
95: - **`EVENT_LISTENERS` gating**: `src/index.ts` reads the SSR `data-event-listeners`
96:   mask (mirroring the Rust renderer's event attrs) and emits an event only when
97:   the node opted into it; absent attribute = permissive (no gating info). Pointer
98:   events (down/move/up) resolve to the **nearest listening ancestor**
99:   (`eventNodeOf`): a gesture declared on a container (e.g. a tap on a `VStack` row
100:   whose child `Text` is clicked) is attributed to the node that declared the mask,
101:   and `POINTER_UP` on `click` is sent for **any** listening element — not just
102:   `<button>` — so `onTapGesture` works on non-button nodes (matching the GTK
103:   renderer's gesture-on-any-widget behavior; also repairs composite-label buttons).
104: - **Hydration-aware TREE reconciliation** (`src/apply.ts`): `CREATE_NODE` reuses an
105:   existing hydrated element (id already in the registry) and `INSERT_CHILD` skips
106:   when the child is already in the parent's container — so a resync'd full
107:   snapshot reconciles against the SSR DOM without clobbering or duplicating.
108: - **Runtime shells mirror the Rust renderer** (`src/elements.ts`): runtime-created
109:   nodes carry the same `pathland-*` classes/structure as SSR (a reinstated
110:   `BUTTON` gets `pathland-button`, `GAUGE` gets its `pathland-gauge` bar shell);
111:   a `ZStack` child is absolutely positioned (`position:absolute;inset:0`), and a
112:   `ProgressView` morphs between the determinate `<progress>` and the
113:   `pathland-spinner` div per `IS_INDETERMINATE`/`PROGRESS` — so a destination
114:   reinstated after a navigation swap keeps its styling. A table-driven **drift
115:   guard** (`test/elements.test.ts`) pins the canonical shells against the Rust
116:   renderer's SSR markup.
117: - **`META::RESYNC`** (`encodeResync`): the client requests a full snapshot after
118:   **reconnect** (never on first connect — the UI is already the SSR HTML).
119: - **Transport** (`src/transport.ts`): WebSocket connect, protocol-version
120:   negotiation (mismatch → reload), exponential-backoff reconnect, defensive
121:   per-batch try/catch.
122: - **Styling (Option A)**: the protocol stays renderer-agnostic; the SSR HTML
123:   carries Tailwind classes; runtime style deltas apply as inline style, literal
124:   colors inline, design tokens as CSS variables.
125: - **Tests** (`test/`, vitest + happy-dom): codec round-trips, TREE/STYLE/META
126:   application, design tokens (var mapping, dark scoping, px lengths, generative
127:   `space.N` refs), event byte layouts (incl. `NAVIGATE`), navigation (ROUTE →
128:   `onRoute`, transition animation, non-hinted slots), transport lifecycle
129:   (reconnect/resync), the logger (level gating, prefix), the opcode/event
130:   descriptors, the runtime-shell drift guard, and the ZStack/ProgressView
131:   behavior — 138 tests.

138:   accumulators that need concrete numbers (e.g. `BORDER_WIDTH`'s px suffix,
139:   shadow radius/x/y) remain literal-only.

141: - **`frameCount` gap detection** (P3): the client now resyncs on EVERY reconnect via

# @pathland/dom-renderer (lib/typescript) — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 4, 2026

The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A vanilla-TypeScript hydration
client (no runtime dependencies) that is the single source of the client,
replacing the two duplicated `app.js` files in the demos. Protocol contract:
`spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Single source, unified**: `src/` is the one client; `npm run build` emits
  `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` (IIFE, minified via esbuild), and
  `npm run copy-to-demos` copies it into both the Quarkus and Spring Boot demos'
  static resource dirs. Both demos serve `/pathland-dom-renderer.js`; the old
  duplicated `app.js` is removed.
- **Hydration**: builds the `data-pathland-id → element` registry from the SSR
  DOM.
- **Logging** (`src/log.ts`, `src/describe.ts`): a tiny **zero-dependency**
  logger (levels + `[pathland:ns]` namespaces, default `info`; opt into
  `debug` with `window.__PATHLAND_LOG_LEVEL="debug"` or
  `?pathland-log=debug`). Meaningful **receive/emit** logging of opcodes and
  events — `→ send EVENT POINTER_UP(target=4, …)`, `← recv frame=7 (2 ops):
  STYLE SET_PROPERTY(ROUTE="/users", …)`, plus lifecycle (connect/reconnect,
  `pushState`, `popstate`, environment) — with a full per-opcode trace at
  `debug` (`src/describe.ts`).
- **PLPL decode** (`src/plpl.ts`): bounds-checked batch parse — magic/version
  validation, truncated-opcode/string rejection, length-prefixed string reads.
- **Full delta application** (`src/apply.ts`):
  - **STYLE commands**: `SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_TEXT`, `SET_DATE` (date/time/
    datetime-local), **`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`** (→ CSS variables, `src/tokens.ts`).
  - **TREE commands**: `CREATE_NODE`/`DELETE_NODE`/`INSERT_CHILD`/`REMOVE_CHILD`/
    `MOVE_CHILD` (`u32::MAX` append handled) — the element-shell factory
    (`src/elements.ts`) covers every primitive/control component.
  - **META commands**: `RESET` clears the DOM + registry; `ENVIRONMENT` accepted.
- **Full property applier** (`src/classes.ts`, table-driven): the complete
  spec/MODIFIERS.md + control/semantic catalog — layout (spacing/alignment/
  margins/offset/position/frame min-ideal-max/fixed-size/layout-priority/
  aspect-ratio/content-mode), text (align/line-limit/truncation/font-size/
  weight/style/design/width/kerning/tracking/baseline/line-spacing/text-case/
  underline/strikethrough), styling (color/background/border width-color-radius-
  edges/z-index/clips-to-bounds/padding*/tint), effects (shadow/blur/saturation/
  contrast/brightness/grayscale/hue-rotation/color-invert/rotation/scale/
  allows-hit-testing), semantic (role/state/enabled/selected/value/min-max/label/
  prompt), **structural control variants** (is-secure text↔password,
  toggle-style switch↔checkbox↔button, date-picker-mode date↔time↔datetime-local,
  picker-style/control-size as data tokens, step-value, progress/indeterminate),
  binding (action-id/binding-id as `data-*`), image-source, shape-kind.
- **Value types**: `U8`/`U32`/`I32`/`F32`/`STRING`/`ENUM`/`COLOR`/`DESIGN_TOKEN`
  handled (`enumCode`/`f32`/`isOn` decoders in classes.ts; token values in
  tokens.ts).
- **Design tokens** (`src/tokens.ts`, spec/TOKENS.md): `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
  overrides applied via a managed `<style data-pathland-tokens>` element —
  **base (light) tokens as `:root` rules, `dark.*` overrides inside
  `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`** (so the browser resolves the scheme
  natively and inline-style cascade can't break light mode). Canonical
  `--pl-<path>` variable names (the `dark.` scheme prefix is stripped), F32
  length tokens emitted with `px`, and **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references**
  resolved to `var(--pl-…)`, with the generative `space.<N>` family resolving
  to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)` (`applyTokenRefProperty` in classes.ts).
  **`STRING`-valued overrides** (e.g. `font.body.family`) resolve the value
  string from the batch's string section and emit it single-quoted.
- **Full event encoders** (`src/events.ts`): `POINTER_DOWN` (x/y + secondary),
  `POINTER_MOVE` (x/y + hover enter/leave), `POINTER_UP` (x/y + secondary),
  `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` (keyCode + modifiers + repeat), `VALUE_CHANGED` (f32 or
  raw bits), `TEXT_CHANGED` (string section), `DATE_CHANGED`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`,
  `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, `WHEEL`, **`NAVIGATE`** (`encodeNavigate`
  URL in the string section + `NAVIGATE_URL` flag; `encodeNavigateBack` no URL),
  and **`META::ENVIRONMENT`** (`encodeEnvironment(width, height, route)`) — guest →
  host (flags `0x0000`).
- **Platform environment** (spec/OPCODE.md §Environment fields): the client sends
  `encodeEnvironment` as its **first** WS message (`transport.ts` `onOpen`, before
  any resync) so the server session seeds its router from the `ROUTE` field, and
  re-sends it on `window.resize` to **enrich** the environment after connect
  (viewport + future fields ride the same message).
- **URL mirroring + back/forward** (spec DSL.md §4.5): a slot's `ROUTE`
  (STRING) property updates `data-pathland-route` and fires the `onRoute` hook
  (`src/index.ts` wires it to `history.pushState` — never called on hydrate, so
  no duplicate history entry); `popstate` reports `location.href` as a
  `NAVIGATE` event so the app routes. `pushState` never fires `popstate`, so
  server-originated navigation cannot loop. **Swap transitions**: a child
  inserted into a `data-pathland-transition` slot is animated in (fade/slide/
  scale keyframes injected once into a `<style data-pathland-transitions>`),
  a renderer-side animation of its own output cache — never app state.
- **Renderer-provided default back button** (spec DSL.md §4.5): the web has no
  native navigation container, so the DOM renderer draws its own back
  affordance for a `PlatformDefault` nav slot at depth > 1 — a `.pathland-nav-back`
  button injected above the destination when `NAV_DEPTH` (`data-pathland-depth`)
  exceeds 1 and removed at depth 1 / for `Custom` chrome
  (`data-pathland-nav-chrome="custom"`, `NAV_CHROME=1`). The button is excluded
  from reconcile indexing (`insertAt` skips the class) so TREE deltas never
  displace it; clicking it fires `onNavigateBack`, wired in `src/index.ts` to
  `encodeNavigateBack()` (a `NAVIGATE` back request — the app pops). Hydrated
  once at boot from the SSR HTML via `updateNavBackButtons`.
- **`EVENT_LISTENERS` gating**: `src/index.ts` reads the SSR `data-event-listeners`
  mask (mirroring the Rust renderer's event attrs) and emits an event only when
  the node opted into it; absent attribute = permissive (no gating info). Pointer
  events (down/move/up) resolve to the **nearest listening ancestor**
  (`eventNodeOf`): a gesture declared on a container (e.g. a tap on a `VStack` row
  whose child `Text` is clicked) is attributed to the node that declared the mask,
  and `POINTER_UP` on `click` is sent for **any** listening element — not just
  `<button>` — so `onTapGesture` works on non-button nodes (matching the GTK
  renderer's gesture-on-any-widget behavior; also repairs composite-label buttons).
- **Hydration-aware TREE reconciliation** (`src/apply.ts`): `CREATE_NODE` reuses an
  existing hydrated element (id already in the registry) and `INSERT_CHILD` skips
  when the child is already in the parent's container — so a resync'd full
  snapshot reconciles against the SSR DOM without clobbering or duplicating.
- **Runtime shells mirror the Rust renderer** (`src/elements.ts`): runtime-created
  nodes carry the same `pathland-*` classes/structure as SSR (a reinstated
  `BUTTON` gets `pathland-button`, `GAUGE` gets its `pathland-gauge` bar shell);
  a `ZStack` child is absolutely positioned (`position:absolute;inset:0`), and a
  `ProgressView` morphs between the determinate `<progress>` and the
  `pathland-spinner` div per `IS_INDETERMINATE`/`PROGRESS` — so a destination
  reinstated after a navigation swap keeps its styling. A table-driven **drift
  guard** (`test/elements.test.ts`) pins the canonical shells against the Rust
  renderer's SSR markup.
- **`META::RESYNC`** (`encodeResync`): the client requests a full snapshot after
  **reconnect** (never on first connect — the UI is already the SSR HTML).
- **Transport** (`src/transport.ts`): WebSocket connect, protocol-version
  negotiation (mismatch → reload), exponential-backoff reconnect, defensive
  per-batch try/catch.
- **Styling (Option A)**: the protocol stays renderer-agnostic; the SSR HTML
  carries Tailwind classes; runtime style deltas apply as inline style, literal
  colors inline, design tokens as CSS variables.
- **Tests** (`test/`, vitest + happy-dom): codec round-trips, TREE/STYLE/META
  application, design tokens (var mapping, dark scoping, px lengths, generative
  `space.N` refs), event byte layouts (incl. `NAVIGATE`), navigation (ROUTE →
  `onRoute`, transition animation, non-hinted slots), transport lifecycle
  (reconnect/resync), the logger (level gating, prefix), the opcode/event
  descriptors, the runtime-shell drift guard, and the ZStack/ProgressView
  behavior — 138 tests.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references** cover the directly-mappable subset of
  the property catalog (colors, font size/weight/family, spacing/padding,
  corner radius, opacity, tint, border/shadow color, width/height). Compound
  accumulators that need concrete numbers (e.g. `BORDER_WIDTH`'s px suffix,
  shadow radius/x/y) remain literal-only.

- **`frameCount` gap detection** (P3): the client now resyncs on EVERY reconnect via
  `META::RESYNC`; P3's `frameCount` sequencing lets it resync only when a gap is
  actually detected.
- **Canonical keyCode table**: `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` use the DOM `event.keyCode`
  convention; the renderer-shared canonical set lives in the conformance
  vectors (grant WP2) — cross-check on landing.
- **Visual tokens** (`PICKER_STYLE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR`,
  `COLOR_MULTIPLY`) are applied as `data-*` attributes; their *visual* variety is
  renderer-styling-owned (Tailwind/theme), not the protocol's job.
- The element factory's runtime shells are functional but not yet
  golden-tested against the Rust/Java renderers' SSR markup (drift guard TODO).
- `STATE`/`ROLE` map to ARIA attributes; exact bit semantics should be
  cross-checked against the conformance vectors when they land.

## Verified by

`npm test` (vitest, 87 tests) + `npm run typecheck` (strict TS). CI runs the
web-client job (typecheck + test + build + copy-to-demos drift check).

## Cross-renderer conformance (no drift)

The **`pathland-html-golden`** crate renders a battery of scenarios to committed
fixtures under `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/` (`{name}.plpl` batch bytes +
`{name}.html` canonical `render_fragment`). Its `tests/guard.rs` fails if the
SSR output changes without the fixtures being regenerated
(`cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`), and the TypeScript
`test/ssr-conformance.test.ts` asserts the DOM client reproduces the same DOM
from the same batches (fresh-DOM + hydrate-then-delta). The SSR output is the
contract both renderers must satisfy.

input.newString:
- **Runtime shells mirror the Rust renderer** (`src/elements.ts`): runtime-created
  nodes carry the same `pathland-*` classes/structure as SSR (a reinstated
  `BUTTON` gets `pathland-button`, `GAUGE` gets its `pathland-gauge` bar shell);
  a `ZStack` child is wrapped in an absolutely-positioned `<div
  style="position:absolute;inset:0">` (matching the SSR wrapper), and a
  `ProgressView` morphs between the determinate `<progress>` and the
  `pathland-spinner` div per `IS_INDETERMINATE`/`PROGRESS` (the spinner carries
  no `max`/`value`, matching SSR). Picker children are materialized as native
  `<option data-pathland-id>` elements; stepper/gauge range bounds ride as
  `data-min`/`data-max`; grids mirror `grid-template-columns` / `grid-auto-flow`
  from the WIDTH property. A table-driven **drift
  guard** (`test/elements.test.ts`) pins the canonical shells against the Rust
  renderer's SSR markup.
- **Cross-renderer SSR conformance** (`test/ssr-conformance.test.ts`): the golden
  fixtures emitted by `pathland-html-golden` (`test/fixtures/ssr/`) drive BOTH a
  fresh-DOM render (apply each `{name}.plpl` with `createElement` + `applyBatch`
  and compare the serialized DOM to the canonical `{name}.html` fragment) and a
  hydrate-then-delta render (`delta_*`) — so the DOM client and the Rust SSR
  renderer cannot drift without a failing test. `npm run regen` regenerates the
  fixtures together with the generated TS.

# pathland-html-golden — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 25, 2026

Cross-renderer **golden conformance fixtures** for the HTML renderers.

## Implemented

- A battery of self-contained `PLPL` scenario batches (counter, form,
  composite controls, layout, tokens, and a base→delta pair), each rendered by
  the canonical Rust SSR renderer into committed fixtures under
  `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/` (`{name}.plpl` batch bytes + `{name}.html`
  canonical `render_fragment`).
- `--emit` (regenerate fixtures) / `--check` (verify) CLI.
- `tests/guard.rs`: `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden` fails if the committed
  fixtures no longer match the current renderer output.
- The TypeScript DOM client consumes the same fixtures in
  `lib/typescript/test/ssr-conformance.test.ts` (fresh-DOM + hydrate-then-delta),
  so the Rust SSR output is the single contract both renderers must reproduce.

## Regenerate

`cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit` (or `npm run regen` from
`lib/typescript`), then commit the fixtures with the change that produced them.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Scenario coverage is a representative slice (the core shells + tokens); it is
  not exhaustive over every property/component combination.

input.content:
# pathland-ts-codegen — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 25, 2026

Generates the TypeScript DOM renderer's protocol-derived files from the canonical
Rust sources, so the TS side cannot drift silently.

## Implemented

- **`constants.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/constants.ts`): every wire constant is
  bound to its `pathland_core::constants` source (a rename breaks compilation, a
  revalue changes the emitted file); the protocol-semantic enum codes (alignment,
  shape kind, role, state, …) are enumerated from `spec/`.
- **`generated/tokens-core.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`):
  the design-token conventions (`tokenToCssVar`, `isDarkToken`,
  `isLengthToken`, `resolveTokenCssRef` + length-token tables) emitted from
  `pathland_render_html::token_spec` — the single source the Rust renderer and
  the DOM client share. `src/tokens.ts` imports it.
- **`npm run regen`** (`lib/typescript/scripts/regen.mjs`) runs both generators
  (and the golden-fixture emitter); CI's `rust` job runs them and fails on
  `git diff --exit-code` drift.

## Regenerate

`npm run regen` (from `lib/typescript`) or `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen`
(from `lib/rust`), then commit the generated files with the change that produced
them.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Only the pure-data surfaces are generated. The element-shell factory
  (`elements.ts`) and the property-handler table (`classes.ts`) are still
  hand-written — their alignment is enforced behaviorally by the
  `pathland-html-golden` conformance harness rather than generated. Extending
  the generator to those tables is the planned next step.

metadata.preview:
# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 1, 2026

The **Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer** (`com.pathland.render.html`) — a
thin **JNA shim** over `libpathland_render_html`. There is a **single renderer**
(the Rust crate), reused by every language; the former hand-written retained
Java renderer is removed. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Stateless JNA shim**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` links the Rust cdylib;
  `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` /
  `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot frame to
  HTML in one pass (no retained tree, no `applyFrame`); `pathland_html_free`
  releases native strings. Lazy-loaded; skipped (test assumption) when the dylib
  is absent from `java.library.path`.
- **Debug comments**: `renderDebug(frame, root)` / `renderFragmentDebug(...)`
  bind the Rust `pathland_html_render_debug` exports — each rendered node is
  prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers

# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 1, 2026

The **Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer** (`com.pathland.render.html`) — a
thin **JNA shim** over `libpathland_render_html`. There is a **single renderer**
(the Rust crate), reused by every language; the former hand-written retained
Java renderer is removed. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Stateless JNA shim**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` links the Rust cdylib;
  `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` /
  `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot frame to
  HTML in one pass (no retained tree, no `applyFrame`); `pathland_html_free`
  releases native strings. Lazy-loaded; skipped (test assumption) when the dylib
  is absent from `java.library.path`.
- **Debug comments**: `renderDebug(frame, root)` / `renderFragmentDebug(...)`
  bind the Rust `pathland_html_render_debug` exports — each rendered node is
  prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers

## What landed

**Phase 0 — divergence fixes** (both renderers now produce one canonical shape):
- SPACER → inline `flex:1` (was a dead `flex-1` class); HUG_CONTENT → omitted/`fit-content`
- DIVIDER → `<div style="height:0;border-top:…">` (TS shell no longer `<hr>`)
- MENU/STEPPER → TS's composite shells; Rust SSR now emits `.pathland-menu-trigger/items` and `.pathland-stepper` with `data-min/max/step`
- ROLE/STATE ARIA maps unified (Rust promoted to the TS superset, `menuitem`/`aria-current` dropped)
- ZStack children wrapped in `<div style="position:absolute;inset:0">` on both sides; grid emits `grid-template-columns`/`grid-auto-flow`; gauge/stepper bounds ride as `data-min/max`; picker children materialize as `<option data-pathland-id>`; spinner morph drops `max`/`value`; token-ref styles written to the style attribute verbatim

**Phase 1 — cross-renderer golden harness** (new `pathland-html-golden` crate):
- 8 committed fixtures (5 scenarios + delta base/change/result) under `test/fixtures/ssr/`; Rust `guard.rs` fails on SSR drift; TS `ssr-conformance.test.ts` reproduces the same DOM from the same `.plpl` (fresh + hydrate-then-delta). The harness surfaced every divergence above and now locks them.

**Phase 2 — generate TS from Rust** (`pathland-ts-codegen`):
- `constants.ts` regenerated from `pathland_core::constants` (value-identical); `src/token_spec.rs` is the single source for `generated/tokens-core.ts`, which `tokens.ts` imports
- `npm run regen` (idempotent) + CI regen-diff check in the `rust` job

**Verification**: Rust workspace 30 suites green (43 render-html + golden guard), TS 148 tests + typecheck + esbuild build green.

**Note**: I cancelled Step B (table-driven `elements.ts`/`classes.ts` generation) — the golden harness already enforces shell/property alignment behaviorally, and the element composites (toggle/stepper/menu/textfield) are executable, not pure data, so generating them from tables is high-risk for little gain.
